Stoatmod Permissions and Role Hierarchy Guide

A command can be syntactically correct and still fail when the bot lacks a permission, cannot see the channel or sits below the target member or role.

Move the Stoatmod role above every ordinary member it needs to moderate and every role it needs to assign. Stoat rejects role assignment, nickname restoration, timeouts, kicks and bans when the acting bot is not high enough in the hierarchy.

Configure Stoatmod Automod, Thresholds and Categories
Configure Stoatmod thresholds, categories, spam, links, images, join protection, nicknames and moderator exemptions.
Treat category scores, specialised protection systems and per-channel scope as separate controls, then verify them together in a controlled test.

The default content-moderation threshold is 90%. Server owners can choose a threshold from 0% to 100%, with optional overrides for individual categories. Percentages are model scores, not calibrated probabilities of harm.

Use include and exclude with a channel or category ID to control automatic-moderation scope. Moderator exemption defaults on. Logging can still occur in spaces excluded from automatic intervention, so test both moderation and audit behaviour.

Stoatmod Warnings and Moderation Cases Guide
Create, inspect and remove Stoatmod warnings and understand how cases interact with escalation and appeals.
Warnings contribute to escalation while cases preserve the server-scoped record. Removing a record and reversing a punishment are not the same operation.
The default policy applies a timeout at three active warnings, a kick at five and a ban at seven. The dashboard can replace this with a staged policy using unique thresholds.

Removing a warning case stops it contributing to warning escalation while retaining its removed state. Removing a non-warning case does not undo a timeout, kick or ban. Use the appeal or appropriate moderation command when the real server state must change.

Stoatmod Mute, Kick and Ban Commands
Use Stoatmod mute, unmute, kick and ban commands with permission, hierarchy and outcome-verification checks.
A command response is only one part of the operation. Verify the member's real state and include a clear reason for every moderation action. Removing a case is the exception.
Mute with a required reason. Put the duration before or after the reason, or omit it for a one-hour mute.
Remove the member from the server.
Ban the member from the server.
Remove the server ban and record the reason for reversal.

Use a member mention or user ID. These forms both mute for 25 minutes: ~mute @member 25m repeated spam and ~mute @member repeated spam 25m. Omitting the duration uses one hour: ~mute @member repeated spam. A reason is always required.
Durations support 25m, 2h, 1h30m and 25 minutes, up to four weeks. Unmute, unban, warn, kick, ban, application decisions and verification bypass also require a reason; case removal does not.
